description: Task: write a Python function solve(nums, target) that returns a list [i, j] of two indices with i < j such that nums[i] + nums[j] == target. The argument nums is a list of integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 2000 and every value between -10**9 and 10**9 inclusive; target is an integer. Each input has exactly one pair of indices whose values add up to target, so the answer is unique. The two indices must be different positions, although the values at them may be equal.

The argument nums is a list of integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 2000 and every value between -10**9 and 10**9 inclusive; target is an integer. Each input has exactly one pair of indices whose values add up to target, so the answer is unique. The two indices must be different positions, although the values at them may be equal.

catalogue.display_name: a hash map of seen values
catalogue.mechanism: scan once, storing each value's index in a dict and looking up target minus the current value
sort (value, index) pairs and move two pointers inwards from both ends
